newsitem.title: UK: Major says will not change policy to get IRA truce.
newsitem.headline: Major says will not change policy to get IRA truce.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major told parliament on Thursday he was not prepared to change the British government's Northern Ireland policy and bargain with IRA guerrillas for a new ceasefire.

Major was answering a question in parliament after the government held talks with Catholic nationalist politicians over new proposals aimed at breaking deadlock over the participation of Sinn Fein, the IRA's political wing, in peace talks.
"We have made it absolutely clear throughout those exchanges that the IRA and Sinn Fein should give up violence and commit themselves to exclusively peaceful means," Major told the House of Commons.
"We have also made it clear that we cannot and we will not change our policy to bargain for a ceasefire," he said.

Major said he was not seeking to delay the peace process. Britain's position for many months has been that Sinn Fein were excluded from multi-party peace talks until the IRA declared a ceasefire. "When Sinn Fein can join the talks depends upon their own actions. We need to see an unequivocal restoration of the ceasefire we need to be able to make a credible judgment that it's lasting," he said.
